The ledger is the application's live record, in memory; a durable audit trail is fed from the action events on the bridge ([S-AXE-5]) or by the application.

**[S-LED-7]** The ledger records acts made through the surface. A change made through the application's own controls appears as a revision move ([S-REV-3]), not as an entry, unless the application routes it through `act`.

**[S-REV-5]** The application MUST re-register (or `reconcile`) whenever anything that feeds an entry's `state`, `value`, or `edit` changes, including transient states: a save in flight, data loading, a modal open. An observation MUST reflect the application's state as of its `rev`. A surface that reports a control available while the application has disabled it is a defect; §5.1 is the shortest way to avoid it for a state that spans the surface.

### 5.2 Transient states

**[S-FRZ-1]** `freeze(reason)` marks the whole surface unavailable for a transient state and returns `thaw`. While frozen, every action reports `{ available: false, reason }` with the freeze's reason in place of its own state (and no `requires` or `handoff`), every field is read-only with that `reason`, no collection can load more, and no entry carries an `index`. Field values remain visible.

**[S-FRZ-2]** `freeze` moves the revision, and so does `thaw`. `observe()` carries a top-level `frozen: { reason }` while frozen and omits it otherwise.

**[S-FRZ-3]** An act during a freeze is `error` with `code: "unavailable"`, `retryable: true`, and `details.reason` (also `details.frozen`), whatever the entry's own state, and no handler runs. A numeric target during a freeze is `not_found`, since no row carries an index; an act planned before the freeze is `conflict` under [S-ACT-2].

**[S-FRZ-4]** Freezes nest and are counted: the newest reason is the one reported, the surface thaws when the last freeze is released, and releasing the same freeze twice does nothing.

## 6. The seam: every control as an AXE action

The reviewer who designed Surface put it in one line: each available Surface entry can be published as an AXE action, so discovery, MCP, kinds, and the audit come for free. An agent reading the manifest or an MCP tool list sees "Draft Jahmyr Gibbs (RB)" and "Lock March", each with its own availability and reason, not one `act` tool with a `target` parameter. The first cut of this seam had that generic action; it is gone.

**[S-AXE-1]** `surfaceActions(surface, { namespace })` returns an action provider (the SDK's `ActionProvider`, registered with `addProvider`) whose set is, in order: `<ns>.observe` (read-only, `risk: none`, `display` over `entries`, and a dynamic affordance per actionable row that names the row's own action with `input: {}` and the observation's `rev` as the affordance's `expectedRev`), `<ns>.ledger` (read-only, `risk: none`, input `{ since?, limit? }`, output `{ ledgerSeq, entries }` with `display` over the entries), and one action per registered entry ([S-AXE-6]), in registration order. Contract v0.2's generic `<ns>.act` is removed; its `target`, `op`, and `input.expectedRev` have no successor, since each action names its entry and op and the revision travels on the envelope ([S-AXE-4]).

**[S-AXE-2]** Refusals map onto the ladder: an unavailable action with `requires` becomes `needs_input` with those `accepts` (and the declared `handoff` as `fallback` when present); one with only a `handoff` becomes `needs_human`; a stale revision is `error` `conflict`; other refusals stay `error` with their reason. A refusal during a freeze ([S-FRZ-3]) is `error` `unavailable` with the freeze's reason and never climbs the ladder, since there is nothing to fulfill or hand off until the freeze lifts. On `/axe/continue`, the application's `fulfill` runs and the act is retried at the current revision; on `/axe/resume`, the act is retried at the current revision. The `state` a continuation or resume carries is the act request, with the entry id as `target`, so a later act lands on the same control whatever the action set has become.

**[S-AXE-3]** The `actor` recorded for an act that arrives through AXE is the authenticated `onBehalfOf` when there is one, else `agent`.

**[S-AXE-4]** Served through AXE, the surface's revision is the site's revision (protocol §21): the server is created with `revision: surface.currentRev`, so every envelope carries `rev`, the protocol's stale check ([P-LIVE-3]) runs before the handler, and `/axe/state` reports the revision. The revision the agent observed travels as the request envelope's `expectedRev` and nowhere else; an entry's action takes none in its `input`. A request without `expectedRev` reaches the surface, which refuses it as `invalid_input` under [S-ACT-3]: every act presents the revision the agent saw.

**[S-AXE-5]** For every act that goes through an entry's action, `/axe/continue`, or `/axe/resume`, run or refused, the bridge MUST emit one action event (`EVENTS.md`, "Action events") named `surface.act`, with `action` the entry's action name, `status` and `errorCode` as the surface returned them, `actor` as recorded in the ledger, and `details: { seq, op, target, revBefore, revAfter, changed }`. Action events reach the server's `onActionEvent` sinks, not its analytics sinks, because they name the actor.

**[S-AXE-6] The action for an entry.** Its `title` is the entry `name` ([S-ENT-1]: the outcome, in the application's words). Its `description` is composed from the kind, the name, the `object`, and the effect, and stays within [P-ACT-7]'s bounds whatever the name's length; it does not carry the availability, which is live ([S-AXE-8]). `readOnly` is false for every kind: an action runs a handler, a field runs a setter, and a collection load changes the view. For an `action` entry, `idempotent`, `reversible`, and `risk` are the `effect`'s ([S-EFF-1]); `input` requires `confirm` (a literal `true`) when the effect declares `confirm`, and takes an optional `text` described by the effect's `text` prompt when it declares one. For a `field` entry, `idempotent` is true (setting the same text twice sets it once), `reversible` and `risk` are the bridge's field options (defaults false and `medium`), and `input` is `{ text }`, required, bounded by `maxLength` or validated by the field's own schema when it has one; a read-only field keeps the same shape and is unavailable ([S-AXE-8]). For a `collection` entry, `idempotent` and `reversible` are false, `risk` is `low`, and `input` is empty. Every entry action's `output` is the act output of [S-ACT-1]: `{ rev, id, actor, changed, seq }`. An action entry that declares a `handoff` at registration declares `humanHandoff: { reasons: [handoff.reason] }`. The op the action performs is fixed by the entry: `TOGGLE` for a `switch`, `CLICK` for any other action role, `TYPE_TEXT` for a field, `SCROLL_DOWN` for a collection.

**[S-AXE-7] Names.** An entry's action is `<ns>.<slug>`. The plain slug of an id is the id lowercased, with every run of characters outside `a-z0-9` replaced by one hyphen, leading and trailing hyphens dropped, and `e-` prefixed when the result is empty or starts with a digit, so `pick:me:Gibbs` is `pick-me-gibbs`, `cell:2026-03` is `cell-2026-03`, and `2026-03` is `e-2026-03`. When the plain slug is `observe`, `ledger`, or `act`, or is already held by a different id, the slug is the plain slug, a hyphen, and a short hash of the exact id (FNV-1a, base 36), with a counter appended in the vanishing case of a second collision. The bridge keeps the map in both directions for its lifetime: `actionNameFor(entryId)` always returns the same name for the same id, an id that leaves and returns keeps its name, and `entryIdFor(actionName)` returns the exact id an action was issued for, or undefined for a name the bridge never issued. `entrySlug(id)` exposes the plain slug alone. Every name produced fits [P-ACT-1]'s pattern.

**[S-AXE-8] Availability.** Every entry action declares an `availability` hook ([P-LIVE-5]) that returns `surface.availability(id)` ([S-OBS-3]): an action's `state` with its `reason`, `requires`, and `handoff`; `{ available: false, reason }` for a read-only field and for a collection that cannot load more; and, while the surface is frozen, `{ available: false, reason }` with the freeze's reason for every entry ([S-FRZ-1]). The manifest carries it as rendered and `/axe/state` serves it live, so an agent sees per control what it can do right now and why not the rest without calling `<ns>.observe`. The hook reads one entry; it MUST NOT take a whole observation, so `/axe/state` over hundreds of rows costs hundreds of lookups, not hundreds of tables.

**[S-AXE-9] Churn and scale.** The action set follows the registry: an entry registered or unregistered is in or out of the manifest, `/axe/state`, and the derived MCP tool list on the next request, without re-registering anything with the server. The set is rebuilt only when `registryVersion()` moved; a `bump` alone reuses the previous set, and within a rebuild an entry object already published keeps its action. Name lookup on invocation is by map, not by scan, so a surface with hundreds of rows invokes in constant time. An entry whose text fails the honesty lint ([P-HON-1]) at build time is not published as an action: the bridge reports it through its `onError` option (default: one warning per entry) and the entry keeps its row in `<ns>.observe`, without an affordance. A retried `idempotencyKey` for an action whose entry has since left the registry (a pick that leaves the board when drafted) is answered from the idempotency store by the server before the name is declared unknown ([P-IDEM-2]), so a lost response is still recoverable.

## 7. Browser agents

Browser-driving agents and screen readers read a control's accessible name, not its registration. Surface mirrors each entry onto the element that receives its interaction, so the page, `observe()`, and the screen reader all read the same outcome-stating name. Two of three gains in the first trial came from the names alone.

**[S-DOM-1] The DOM mirror.** The rules below hold for every entry that has a control on screen.

1. An entry's `name` states the outcome in the application's own words ("Draft Jahmyr Gibbs (RB)", "Lock March", "Load more players"). It MUST NOT name the widget ("button", "Draft button"), repeat the `role`, or carry the state ("disabled", "already drafted"): the role is `role`, the state is `state`. The same string is the control's accessible name and the `name` in `observe()`.
2. The element that receives the entry's interaction (the button, the input, the scrolling container) carries these attributes, and no other element in the document carries its `data-surface-id`:

   | Attribute             | Value                                    | When                                     |
   | --------------------- | ---------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
   | `aria-label`          | the entry `name`                         | always                                   |
   | `data-surface-id`     | the entry `id`                           | always; exactly one element per entry    |
   | `data-surface-kind`   | `action`, `field`, or `collection`       | always                                   |
   | `data-surface-object` | the entry `object`                       | when the entry has one                   |
   | `aria-disabled`       | `true`                                   | an action whose `state` is not available |
   | `aria-readonly`       | `true`                                   | a read-only field                        |
   | `data-surface-reason` | the `reason`, in the application's words | with `aria-disabled` or `aria-readonly`  |

   Collections carry the common set only.

3. `surfaceAttributes(entry)` returns that set as strings from a registered entry or an observed row; `useSurfaceProps(entry, deps)` (`@axe/surface/react`) registers the entry like `useSurface` and returns the set as props, with `aria-disabled` and `aria-readonly` as booleans. An application that uses either MUST render every attribute returned on that element and MUST NOT replace `aria-label` or `data-surface-id` with other values. An application that renders by hand SHOULD carry the same set.
4. The mirror reports; it does not disable [S-RULE-1]. The helper sets `aria-disabled`, never `disabled`, so the application keeps its own disabling logic, and an `aria-disabled` control stays focusable, so a screen reader reaches the reason beside it.

**[S-DOM-2]** `expose(window)` publishes `observe`, `act`, `ledger`, and `rev` at `window.__surface` for agents that drive the page.

**[S-DOM-3] The selector contract.** `surfaceSelector(id)` returns `[data-surface-id="<id>"]` with the id as a double-quoted CSS string: backslashes and double quotes are escaped with a backslash, a newline becomes `\a `, and everything else (colons, spaces, dots, brackets) is left as it is. On a page that follows [S-DOM-1], `document.querySelector(surfaceSelector(row.id))` MUST return the control for `row.id` from any observation, whatever the id contains. Ids are stable [S-ACT-5], so a selector computed from one observation still finds the control after the revision moves; a stale selector is never an error, a stale act is [S-ACT-2].

**[S-DOM-4] One-line description.** `describeEntry(entry)` returns one line of plain text: the `name`, a colon, then the entry's availability in the application's words (`available`, or `unavailable, <reason>`; for a field `editable` or `read only, <reason>`, followed by its value and length; for a collection what is loaded and whether it can load more), and for an action a semicolon and its effect (`mutates <state>`, `idempotent` when set, `reversible` or `not reversible`, `risk <level>`, `confirm required` when set): "Draft Jahmyr Gibbs (RB): unavailable, already drafted by another team; mutates draft, reversible, risk medium". It is agent-read text [S-AV-4]. Applications MAY render it as `aria-description` on the control or log it beside each act; the helper does not render it by default.

## Provenance

[S-ACT-6] to [S-ACT-8], [S-REV-5], and the rules of §5.2 came from two defects found on a real planning application in the first staging trial, both in the seam between Surface and the application: an act whose `target` was `null` matched a row that was not actionable, and the table kept reporting cells editable while the application had frozen editing during a save, so an act ran into the frozen UI. Both were fixed in the application and became rules of the contract here, so the next application does not find them again.

# spec/KINDS.md

# AXE Well-Known Kinds

**Version:** `axe/0.1`. Normative. Schemas in this file are generated into [`schemas/kinds/`](./schemas/kinds/) from `@axe/core/kinds` and a test asserts they match.

A **kind** names the type of payload an agent can submit to satisfy a `needs_input` requirement. Well-known kinds exist so that an agent's wallet or credential store can fulfill a requirement automatically: when a site asks for `payment.ach-debit`, every conforming agent knows the shape without reading prose.

Rules:

**[K-1]** Kind names are namespace-dot-name, kebab-case: `payment.ach-debit`. Well-known namespaces are `payment`, `identity`, `document`, `contact`, and `consent`. Sites MUST NOT define new kinds in these namespaces.

**[K-2]** Custom kinds MUST be named `x-<org>.<name>`, for example `x-oakridge.guarantor-form`. A custom kind's schema MUST NOT be structurally equivalent to a well-known kind's schema (see protocol §18.2, [P-HON-5]).

**[K-3]** In an `accepts[]` entry for a well-known kind, `schema` MUST be the registry schema below or a restriction of it: the site MAY drop optional members, tighten enums, or add `format` constraints. It MUST NOT add required members or relax types.

**[K-4]** `sensitive` defaults given below are the minimum. A site MAY mark any kind `sensitive: true`; it MUST NOT mark a kind listed as sensitive below as `sensitive: false`.

**[K-5]** Payloads are validated by the server on `/axe/continue` against the entry's `schema`. Validation failures return `invalid_input` and do not consume the continuation token.

**[K-6]** Servers MUST NOT log payloads of sensitive kinds and MUST NOT emit them in events. Continuation tokens SHOULD expire within 15 minutes when any accepted kind is sensitive.

All schemas are `"type": "object"` with `"additionalProperties": false`. Strings are non-empty unless noted. Money is a number in major units with an ISO 4217 `currency`.

## payment

### `payment.card`

A tokenized card from the agent's wallet. The token is issued by a payment service provider the site accepts; the raw PAN never appears. Sensitive.

| Member              | Type                         | Required | Meaning                                                     |
| ------------------- | ---------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `token`             | string                       | yes      | PSP-issued single-use or network token.                     |
| `provider`          | string                       | yes      | PSP identifier, e.g. `stripe`, `adyen`, `braintree`.        |
| `brand`             | string                       | no       | Card network, lowercase: `visa`, `mastercard`, `amex`, ...  |
| `last4`             | string, pattern `^[0-9]{4}$` | no       | For display and confirmation.                               |
| `expMonth`          | integer 1–12                 | no       |                                                             |
| `expYear`           | integer                      | no       | Four digits.                                                |
| `billingPostalCode` | string                       | no       |                                                             |
| `amount`            | number ≥ 0                   | no       | Amount the user authorized, when the requirement names one. |
| `currency`          | string, pattern `^[A-Z]{3}$` | no       |                                                             |

### `payment.ach-debit`

Authorization for a one-time ACH debit from a US bank account. Sensitive.

| Member              | Type                            | Required | Meaning                                                     |
| ------------------- | ------------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `accountHolderName` | string                          | yes      |                                                             |
| `routingNumber`     | string, pattern `^[0-9]{9}$`    | yes      | ABA routing number.                                         |
| `accountNumber`     | string, pattern `^[0-9]{4,17}$` | yes      |                                                             |
| `accountType`       | `checking` \| `savings`         | yes      |                                                             |
| `amount`            | number ≥ 0                      | yes      | Amount authorized.                                          |
| `currency`          | string, pattern `^[A-Z]{3}$`    | yes      | `USD` for ACH.                                              |
| `authorizedAt`      | date-time                       | yes      | When the user gave authorization.                           |
| `authorizationText` | string                          | yes      | The exact text the user agreed to. Required by NACHA rules. |

### `payment.wire-confirmation`

Confirmation that the user sent a wire transfer following the site's `accepts[].instructions`. Not sensitive.

| Member            | Type                         | Required | Meaning                      |
| ----------------- | ---------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------- |
| `referenceNumber` | string                       | yes      | Bank reference or IMAD/OMAD. |
| `amount`          | number ≥ 0                   | yes      |                              |
| `currency`        | string, pattern `^[A-Z]{3}$` | yes      |                              |
| `sentAt`          | date-time                    | yes      |                              |
| `bankName`        | string                       | no       | Sending bank.                |

### `payment.invoice`

Request to be invoiced on net terms instead of paying now. The site decides whether to grant terms. Not sensitive.

| Member                | Type            | Required | Meaning                                 |
| --------------------- | --------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------- |
| `companyName`         | string          | yes      |                                         |
| `billingEmail`        | string, `email` | yes      |                                         |
| `purchaseOrderNumber` | string          | no       |                                         |
| `netTermsDays`        | integer 0–180   | no       | Requested terms; the site may override. |
| `taxId`               | string          | no       | VAT or EIN when the site requires it.   |

## identity

### `identity.government-id`

Details from a government-issued identity document. Sensitive.

| Member           | Type                                                                   | Required | Meaning                     |
| ---------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------- |
| `documentType`   | `passport` \| `drivers-license` \| `national-id` \| `residence-permit` | yes      |                             |
| `documentNumber` | string                                                                 | yes      |                             |
| `issuingCountry` | string, pattern `^[A-Z]{2}$`                                           | yes      | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.         |
| `fullName`       | string                                                                 | yes      | As printed on the document. |
| `dateOfBirth`    | date                                                                   | no       |                             |
| `expiresOn`      | date                                                                   | no       |                             |

### `identity.date-of-birth`

| Member        | Type | Required |
| ------------- | ---- | -------- |
| `dateOfBirth` | date | yes      |

Sensitive.

### `identity.ssn-last-4`

| Member  | Type                         | Required |
| ------- | ---------------------------- | -------- |
| `last4` | string, pattern `^[0-9]{4}$` | yes      |

Sensitive.

## document

Sites SHOULD restrict `mimeType` with an `enum` in their `accepts[].schema` when only some types are accepted, and state a size limit in `accepts[].description`.

### `document.url`

A document the site fetches from a URL the agent controls or the user has shared. Not sensitive by default; sites MUST mark it sensitive when the document is (a transcript, a medical record).

| Member      | Type          | Required | Meaning                                                 |
| ----------- | ------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
| `url`       | string, `uri` | yes      | HTTPS. The site fetches it once; it MAY be short-lived. |
| `mimeType`  | string        | yes      | e.g. `application/pdf`.                                 |
| `filename`  | string        | no       |                                                         |
| `sizeBytes` | integer ≥ 0   | no       |                                                         |

### `document.base64`

Inline upload. Sites SHOULD state the maximum size; the SDK enforces a 10 MiB default on the decoded size.

| Member          | Type   | Required | Meaning                              |
| --------------- | ------ | -------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `filename`      | string | yes      |                                      |
| `mimeType`      | string | yes      |                                      |
| `contentBase64` | string | yes      | Standard base64, no data URL prefix. |

## contact

Not sensitive by default. Sites collecting contact data for a minor or in a regulated context MUST mark it sensitive.

### `contact.email`

| Member  | Type            | Required |
| ------- | --------------- | -------- |
| `email` | string, `email` | yes      |

### `contact.phone`

| Member          | Type                                   | Required | Meaning |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- |
| `phone`         | string, pattern `^\+[1-9][0-9]{6,14}$` | yes      | E.164.  |
| `canReceiveSms` | boolean                                | no       |         |

### `contact.address`

| Member       | Type                         | Required | Meaning                         |
| ------------ | ---------------------------- | -------- | ------------------------------- |
| `line1`      | string                       | yes      |                                 |
| `line2`      | string                       | no       |                                 |
| `city`       | string                       | yes      |                                 |
| `region`     | string                       | no       | State, province, or prefecture. |
| `postalCode` | string                       | no       |                                 |
| `country`    | string, pattern `^[A-Z]{2}$` | yes      | ISO 3166-1 alpha-2.             |

## consent

### `consent.terms`

Acknowledgment of one specific policy version for one specific scope. See protocol [P-HON-6]. Not sensitive, but agents SHOULD show the policy to the user before fulfilling.

| Member          | Type          | Required | Meaning                                                                 |
| --------------- | ------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `policyUrl`     | string, `uri` | yes      | The document the user is agreeing to.                                   |
| `policyVersion` | string        | yes      | Exact version identifier or date of the document.                       |
| `scope`         | string        | yes      | What the consent covers, e.g. `rental-application-background-check`.    |
| `acceptedAt`    | date-time     | yes      |                                                                         |
| `acceptedBy`    | string        | no       | Name or identifier of the person consenting, when the site requires it. |

The `accepts[]` entry for a `consent.terms` requirement SHOULD carry, in `instructions`, the policy title and a one-sentence summary of what is being agreed to, so the agent can relay it.

## Adding to this registry

The registry is governed informally in v0 (see `ROADMAP.md`). Proposals add a section here, a definition in `@axe/core/kinds`, a row in `VOCABULARY.md`, and a regenerated schema, in one change.

# spec/EVENTS.md

# AXE Events

**Version:** event `schemaVersion` `1`, shipped with `axe/0.1`. Normative for servers built with the SDK; recommended for other implementations. The JSON Schema is [`schemas/event.schema.json`](./schemas/event.schema.json).

Every request that reaches an action, a continuation, a resume, or a poll produces exactly one event. Events are the Webmaster Tools half of AXE: they answer which agents call you, which actions they use, where the ladder falls to a human, and how long you take. They contain **no personally identifiable information and no payloads**, by construction: the type has no field that could carry them.

## Shape

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "ts": "2026-09-23T18:41:12.204Z",
  "action": "applications.submit",
  "status": "needs_input",
  "ladder": "needs_input",
  "agent": { "vendor": "Acme", "name": "AcmeAgent", "version": "2.1.0" },
  "latencyMs": 184,
  "kind": "payment.ach-debit",
  "errorCode": null,
  "tenant": "oakridge"
}
```

| Member          | Type                                                                                       | Required | Meaning                                                                                                    |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `schemaVersion` | integer                                                                                    | yes      | `1`.                                                                                                       |
| `ts`            | date-time                                                                                  | yes      | When the response was produced.                                                                            |
| `action`        | string                                                                                     | yes      | The action name. For a continue, resume, or poll it is the _originating_ action, recovered from the token. |
| `status`        | `ok` \| `needs_input` \| `needs_human` \| `pending` \| `error`                             | yes      | The `status` of the result envelope returned.                                                              |
| `ladder`        | `ok` \| `needs_input` \| `continued` \| `needs_human` \| `resumed` \| `pending` \| `error` | yes      | Which rung produced this event. See below.                                                                 |
| `agent`         | `{ vendor?, name?, version? }` or `null`                                                   | yes      | From `context.agent`, else parsed from `User-Agent` when it follows the recommended form, else `null`.     |
| `latencyMs`     | integer ≥ 0                                                                                | yes      | Server-side wall time from request receipt to response.                                                    |
| `kind`          | string or `null`                                                                           | yes      | On `continued`: the kind submitted. On `needs_input`: the first accepted kind. Otherwise `null`.           |
| `errorCode`     | error code or `null`                                                                       | yes      | `error.code` when `status` is `error`.                                                                     |
| `tenant`        | string or `null`                                                                           | yes      | Tenant id on platforms, else `null`.                                                                       |

## Ladder semantics

`ladder` records _which endpoint and outcome_ produced the event, so that funnels can be computed without joining requests.

| Endpoint              | Result `status` | `ladder`                                                              |
| --------------------- | --------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `/axe/actions/{name}` | `ok`            | `ok`                                                                  |
| `/axe/actions/{name}` | `needs_input`   | `needs_input`                                                         |
| `/axe/actions/{name}` | `needs_human`   | `needs_human`                                                         |
| `/axe/actions/{name}` | `pending`       | `pending`                                                             |
| `/axe/actions/{name}` | `error`         | `error`                                                               |
| `/axe/continue`       | any             | `continued`                                                           |
| `/axe/resume`         | any             | `resumed`                                                             |
| `/axe/poll/{token}`   | any             | `pending` while pending; the terminal status's ladder value otherwise |

For `continued` and `resumed` events, `status` carries the outcome, so "continues that succeeded" is `ladder = 'continued' AND status = 'ok'`.

## Rules

**[E-1]** Servers MUST emit exactly one event per handled request to an action, continue, resume, or poll endpoint. Manifest and index fetches do not produce events.

**[E-2]** Events MUST NOT contain `input`, `output`, `payload`, `state`, tokens, `onBehalfOf`, `sessionId`, IP addresses, or any header value other than the parsed `agent` fields.

**[E-3]** Events MUST be emitted after the response is determined and MUST NOT delay the response; sinks are invoked asynchronously and a failing sink MUST NOT affect the result.

**[E-4]** Servers MUST include `schemaVersion` so consumers can migrate.

## Action events

A request event says that an action was called and how it went. It cannot say what the action did, or for whom, because [E-2] forbids exactly that. Some actions have to: an action that changes an application's state on a person's behalf owes that person a record, with attribution. Action events are that record. A handler emits one with `emit` on its context; the server stamps it and delivers it to the `onActionEvent` sinks, a channel separate from the analytics `onEvent` sinks, so the two never mix. The JSON Schema is [`schemas/action-event.schema.json`](./schemas/action-event.schema.json).

```json
{
  "schemaVersion": 1,
  "ts": "2026-09-23T18:41:12.204Z",
  "action": "board.pick-me-gibbs",
  "event": "surface.act",
  "status": "ok",
  "errorCode": null,
  "actor": "dana",
  "details": {
    "seq": 12,
    "op": "CLICK",
    "target": "pick:me:Gibbs",
    "revBefore": 7,
    "revAfter": 8,
    "changed": ["pick:me:Gibbs"]
  },
  "tenant": null
}
```

| Member          | Type                                                           | Required | Meaning                                                                                              |
| --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `schemaVersion` | integer                                                        | yes      | `1`.                                                                                                 |
| `ts`            | date-time                                                      | yes      | When the event was emitted.                                                                          |
| `action`        | string                                                         | yes      | The action whose handler emitted it; for a continue or resume, the originating action.               |
| `event`         | string                                                         | yes      | What happened, as a dotted name in the action's namespace: `surface.act`.                            |
| `status`        | `ok` \| `needs_input` \| `needs_human` \| `pending` \| `error` | yes      | Outcome of the work the event records. Defaults to `ok`.                                             |
| `errorCode`     | error code or `null`                                           | yes      | The code when `status` is `error`.                                                                   |
| `actor`         | string or `null`                                               | yes      | Who the work was done as, in the application's terms. `null` when the action has no actor.           |
| `details`       | object                                                         | yes      | What the action chooses to record: identifiers, revisions, sequence numbers. Empty object when none. |
| `tenant`        | string or `null`                                               | yes      | Tenant id on platforms, else `null`.                                                                 |

**[E-5]** A handler, continuation, resume, or poll MAY emit any number of action events through `emit`. The server MUST stamp each with `schemaVersion`, `ts`, `action`, and `tenant`, and deliver it to the `onActionEvent` sinks only. Action events are not request events: they do not count toward [E-1] and MUST NOT be delivered to `onEvent` sinks.

**[E-6]** An action event MAY name the `actor`. It MUST NOT contain `input`, `output`, `payload`, `state`, tokens, `sessionId`, IP addresses, or header values; `details` is for identifiers, revisions, and sequence numbers that let a reader find the record in the application, not for the record itself.

**[E-7]** Emitting MUST NOT delay the response; sinks are invoked asynchronously and a failing sink MUST NOT affect the result.

`spec/SURFACE.md` [S-AXE-4] is the first use: the Surface bridge emits one `surface.act` event per act, run or refused, with the actor and the ledger `seq`.

## Sinks

`@axe/core/events` ships three sinks that accept `AXEEvent` objects: `consoleSink()` (one JSON line per event on stdout), `jsonlFileSink(path)` (append-only JSON lines), and `otelSink({ meter, tracer? })` (an `axe.requests` counter with `action`, `status`, `ladder`, `vendor`, and `tenant` attributes, an `axe.latency` histogram in milliseconds, and an optional span per event). Any function `(event: AXEEvent) => void | Promise<void>` is a sink. `consoleSink()` and `jsonlFileSink(path)` also accept action events, so they can be passed to `onActionEvent`; `otelSink` is for request events only.

`docs/analytics.md` holds the day-one queries against this shape.

# spec/VOCABULARY.md

# AXE Vocabulary

This file is the canonical list of every name that appears on the wire, in the SDK's public API, in the CLI, and in the derived MCP server. Every other document, every package, and every test refers to these names and nothing else.

**This file is the source of truth for code.** `scripts/gen-vocabulary.mjs` parses the tables below and generates `packages/core/src/vocabulary.ts`, exported as `WIRE` from `@axe/core/vocabulary`. A test regenerates the file and fails if it differs from what is committed. A second test (the drift test in `@axe/testing`) scans every Markdown page in `spec/`, `docs/`, and the root `README.md` and fails if an inline code span that looks like a wire name is not in this file, or if a name in this file is never mentioned in the docs or never used in source.

Rules for editing:

- One row per name. Names are exact, including case.
- `Key` is the TypeScript property under `WIRE.<category>`; it is camelCase and unique within its category.
- Do not rename a shipped name before 1.0 without a `DECISIONS.md` entry and a changeset.

## Protocol

| Category | Key     | Name      | Where                                                        | Meaning                                                                     |
| -------- | ------- | --------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| protocol | version | `axe/0.1` | manifest `protocol`, index `protocol`, `AXE-Protocol` header | The protocol version implemented by this SDK. Format `axe/<major>.<minor>`. |

## Paths

| Category | Key           | Name                          | Where | Meaning                                                                                                                   |
| -------- | ------------- | ----------------------------- | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| path     | manifest      | `/.well-known/axe.json`       | HTTP  | Primary manifest location. `GET` returns the manifest.                                                                    |
| path     | manifestAlias | `/axe/manifest`               | HTTP  | Secondary manifest location for hosts that cannot serve `.well-known`.                                                    |
| path     | index         | `/.well-known/axe-index.json` | HTTP  | Platform index of tenant manifests.                                                                                       |
| path     | actions       | `/axe/actions`                | HTTP  | Prefix for action invocation. `POST /axe/actions/{name}` invokes; `GET` returns the definition.                           |
| path     | continue      | `/axe/continue`               | HTTP  | `POST` to satisfy a `needs_input` requirement.                                                                            |
| path     | resume        | `/axe/resume`                 | HTTP  | `POST` after a human handoff completes.                                                                                   |
| path     | poll          | `/axe/poll`                   | HTTP  | Prefix for the SDK's default `pending` poll URLs: `GET /axe/poll/{token}`.                                                |
| path     | state         | `/axe/state`                  | HTTP  | `GET` returns the live state: the current `rev` and every action's `availability`. Served with `Cache-Control: no-store`. |

## Headers

| Category | Key             | Name               | Where                     | Meaning                                                                                 |
| -------- | --------------- | ------------------ | ------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| header   | protocol        | `AXE-Protocol`     | HTTP response and request | Protocol version. Servers send it on every response; agents may send it on requests.    |
| header   | manifest        | `AXE-Manifest`     | HTTP response             | Absolute URL of the manifest, for sites that cannot serve `.well-known`.                |
| header   | retryAfter      | `Retry-After`      | HTTP response             | Seconds to wait, on `429` and on `pending` results.                                     |
| header   | rateLimitPolicy | `RateLimit-Policy` | HTTP response             | Declared rate limit, emitted when `policies.rateLimit` is set, e.g. `60;w=60`.          |
| header   | authorization   | `Authorization`    | HTTP request              | `Bearer <token>` for `site` and `user` auth modes.                                      |
| header   | userAgent       | `User-Agent`       | HTTP request              | Agent self-identification, e.g. `AcmeAgent/2.1 (+https://acme.example/agent; axe/0.1)`. |
| header   | contentType     | `Content-Type`     | HTTP                      | Always `application/json` for AXE requests and responses.                               |

## Discovery hints

| Category | Key         | Name           | Where         | Meaning                                                                   |
| -------- | ----------- | -------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| link     | manifestRel | `axe-manifest` | HTML `<head>` | `<link rel="axe-manifest" href="...">` points to the manifest.            |
| robots   | manifest    | `AXE-Manifest` | `robots.txt`  | `AXE-Manifest: <url>` directive. A hint, not access control.              |
| robots   | index       | `AXE-Index`    | `robots.txt`  | `AXE-Index: <url>` directive pointing at a platform index.                |
| query    | handoff     | `axe_handoff`  | handoff `url` | Query parameter the SDK appends to a handoff URL carrying the handoff id. |

## Result statuses

| Category | Key        | Name          | Where           | Meaning                                                                                   |
| -------- | ---------- | ------------- | --------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| status   | ok         | `ok`          | result `status` | The action completed. `output` is present.                                                |
| status   | needsInput | `needs_input` | result `status` | The action needs something the agent may be able to provide. `accepts` lists the options. |
| status   | needsHuman | `needs_human` | result `status` | A human must act on the site. `handoff` is present.                                       |
| status   | pending    | `pending`     | result `status` | Long-running work. Poll `pollUrl` after `retryAfter` seconds.                             |
| status   | error      | `error`       | result `status` | The action failed. `error` is present.                                                    |

## Error codes

| Category | Key          | Name            | Where        | Meaning                                                                                                         |
| -------- | ------------ | --------------- | ------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| error    | invalidInput | `invalid_input` | `error.code` | Input or payload failed schema validation. `details.issues` names each path.                                    |
| error    | unauthorized | `unauthorized`  | `error.code` | Credentials are missing or invalid for the action's `auth` mode.                                                |
| error    | forbidden    | `forbidden`     | `error.code` | Credentials are valid but this principal may not perform the action.                                            |
| error    | notFound     | `not_found`     | `error.code` | Unknown action, unknown token, or a referenced entity does not exist.                                           |
| error    | conflict     | `conflict`      | `error.code` | State conflict: idempotency key reused with different input, token already consumed, handoff not yet completed. |
| error    | rateLimited  | `rate_limited`  | `error.code` | Too many requests. `Retry-After` is set.                                                                        |
| error    | unavailable  | `unavailable`   | `error.code` | Temporarily unavailable. Retry later.                                                                           |
| error    | internal     | `internal`      | `error.code` | Unexpected server failure.                                                                                      |
| error    | unsupported  | `unsupported`   | `error.code` | Unsupported protocol major version or unsupported feature.                                                      |

## Ladder (event) values

| Category | Key        | Name          | Where          | Meaning                                                                                |
| -------- | ---------- | ------------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| ladder   | ok         | `ok`          | event `ladder` | An action or continuation completed with `ok`.                                         |
| ladder   | needsInput | `needs_input` | event `ladder` | An action returned `needs_input`.                                                      |
| ladder   | continued  | `continued`   | event `ladder` | A `/axe/continue` request was processed (the resulting `status` is on the same event). |
| ladder   | needsHuman | `needs_human` | event `ladder` | An action or continuation returned `needs_human`.                                      |
| ladder   | resumed    | `resumed`     | event `ladder` | A `/axe/resume` request was processed.                                                 |
| ladder   | pending    | `pending`     | event `ladder` | An action returned `pending`.                                                          |
| ladder   | error      | `error`       | event `ladder` | An action, continuation, or resume returned `error`.                                   |

## Enumerations on actions and display

| Category    | Key          | Name            | Where                                | Meaning                                                                                  |
| ----------- | ------------ | --------------- | ------------------------------------ | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| risk        | none         | `none`          | action `risk`                        | Reading public data. Nothing changes.                                                    |
| risk        | low          | `low`           | action `risk`                        | Small, easily reversed change (save a search, add to a waitlist).                        |
| risk        | medium       | `medium`        | action `risk`                        | Commits the user to something reversible (a booking with free cancellation).             |
| risk        | high         | `high`          | action `risk`                        | Money, legal commitment, identity, or hard-to-reverse effects.                           |
| authMode    | none         | `none`          | action `auth`, manifest `auth.modes` | No credentials required.                                                                 |
| authMode    | site         | `site`          | action `auth`, manifest `auth.modes` | The agent authenticates with an API key.                                                 |
| authMode    | user         | `user`          | action `auth`, manifest `auth.modes` | The agent acts for an authenticated end user.                                            |
| displayKind | list         | `list`          | `display.kind`                       | A list of comparable items at `display.items`.                                           |
| displayKind | item         | `item`          | `display.kind`                       | A single item described by `display.item`.                                               |
| displayKind | table        | `table`         | `display.kind`                       | A list best shown as rows and columns.                                                   |
| displayKind | status       | `status`        | `display.kind`                       | The state of one thing (an order, an application).                                       |
| displayKind | document     | `document`      | `display.kind`                       | A long text or file the agent should summarize or link.                                  |
| format      | text         | `text`          | `attributes[].format`                | Plain text.                                                                              |
| format      | number       | `number`        | `attributes[].format`                | A number, no unit.                                                                       |
| format      | currency     | `currency`      | `attributes[].format`                | Money; the value is a number and the currency comes from `price` or the attribute label. |
| format      | date         | `date`          | `attributes[].format`                | ISO 8601 date.                                                                           |
| format      | datetime     | `datetime`      | `attributes[].format`                | ISO 8601 date-time.                                                                      |
| format      | boolean      | `boolean`       | `attributes[].format`                | True or false.                                                                           |
| format      | area         | `area`          | `attributes[].format`                | Area in square feet unless the label says otherwise.                                     |
| format      | distance     | `distance`      | `attributes[].format`                | Distance; the unit is stated in the label.                                               |
| format      | duration     | `duration`      | `attributes[].format`                | ISO 8601 duration or minutes as a number.                                                |
| format      | list         | `list`          | `attributes[].format`                | An array of short strings.                                                               |
| compare     | higherBetter | `higher-better` | `attributes[].compare`               | Larger values are preferable when comparing.                                             |
| compare     | lowerBetter  | `lower-better`  | `attributes[].compare`               | Smaller values are preferable when comparing.                                            |
| compare     | neutral      | `neutral`       | `attributes[].compare`               | No ordering preference.                                                                  |
| period      | once         | `once`          | `price.period`                       | One-time price.                                                                          |
| period      | hour         | `hour`          | `price.period`                       | Price per hour.                                                                          |
| period      | day          | `day`           | `price.period`                       | Price per day.                                                                           |
| period      | month        | `month`         | `price.period`                       | Price per month.                                                                         |
| period      | year         | `year`          | `price.period`                       | Price per year.                                                                          |
| tone        | formal       | `formal`        | `brand.tone`                         | Formal register when the agent speaks for the site.                                      |
| tone        | neutral      | `neutral`       | `brand.tone`                         | Neutral register.                                                                        |
| tone        | casual       | `casual`        | `brand.tone`                         | Casual register.                                                                         |

| Category | Key                     | Name                        | Where            | Meaning                                                         |
